scored_features.gate_reasoning: G1: TRUE — 'Sub cvd (sub_cvd)' is listed among the trial_measured_features so the feature is observed in the dataset. G2: TRUE — the hypothesis specifies plausible pathophysiologic mechanisms (fixed atherothrombotic/pump-failure events less responsive to BP lowering and increased susceptibility to hypotension-related ischemia/decompensation). G3: TRUE — the hypothesis claims the treatment acts differently (attenuated benefit and increased harm) in patients with prior/active CVD rather than simply more baseline risk, i.e., a plausible effect-modifying pathophysiology is proposed. G4: FALSE — large RCT subgroup analyses (including SPRINT reports) have not demonstrated robust, consistent treatment-by-prior-CVD interactions for the primary CV composite, so specific trial-backed interaction evidence is lacking; G4 FALSE — cascade: G5 also FALSE. G5: FALSE — because G4 failed, there is insufficient literature support to justify a clearly actionable, evidence-based subgroup policy in routine practice.
scored_features.justification: Decisive gate: G4 FALSE — although the mechanism is biologically plausible (G2,G3 TRUE), RCT subgroup evidence for a meaningful CVD-by-treatment interaction is lacking, so it fails at the literature-evidence gate.

G5: FALSE — without solid RCT evidence for a stage-dependent interaction, the subgroup recommendations are not fully evidence-backed for clinical decision rules.
scored_features.justification: Decisive gate: G4 FALSE — although CKD-related mechanisms and plausible stage-dependent effects are described (G2/G3 TRUE), the trial literature does not convincingly confirm the specific stage-by-treatment interaction proposed.

scored_features.justification: Decisive gate: G3 FALSE — the hypothesis correctly emphasizes mediators (achieved BP, medication class, access) rather than a direct PD/PK difference, so it does not meet the standard for a genuine treatment effect modifier in this framework.

G2: TRUE — the hypothesis gives physiologic mechanisms (greater achievable BP reduction, pressure-sensitive event types, arterial stiffness/frailty altering harm thresholds) linking baseline SBP to differential treatment effects. G3: FALSE — most of the proposed interaction operates through achievable on‑treatment SBP separation and baseline absolute risk (an absolute‑risk amplifier/mediator) rather than a distinct PD/PK change in how the treatment pharmacologically acts, so it does not clearly qualify as a genuine treatment effect modifier under the strict gate definition; G3 FALSE — cascade: G4 and G5 also FALSE. G4: FALSE — RCTs show larger absolute benefits at higher baseline risk/pressure largely explained by greater BP lowering, but they do not robustly demonstrate a biological treatment-by-baseline-SBP interaction beyond this mediator effect. G5: FALSE — without a specific, literature-proven biological interaction, prescriptive SBP-based treatment rules beyond usual clinical judgment are not fully evidence-backed by RCT interaction data.
scored_features.justification: Decisive gate: G3 FALSE — the interaction is primarily driven by achievable BP lowering and baseline absolute risk (mediators), so it fails the requirement for a distinct biological effect-modifying mechanism.

scored_features.gate_reasoning: G1: TRUE — 'age' is a recorded feature in the trial dataset. G2: TRUE — the hypothesis specifies biologic and physiologic pathways (frailty, physiologic reserve, susceptibility to adverse events like falls/syncope/AKI, competing mortality) that mechanistically link age/frailty to differential net treatment effect. G3: TRUE — the hypothesis claims a genuine effect modification whereby fitter older adults have greater absolute benefit while frail elders may incur more harms and less benefit, i.e., age operates via physiologic tolerance and competing risks to change the net effect rather than being only an absolute-risk amplifier. G4: FALSE — although RCTs (including SPRINT) show benefit in older adults overall, robust RCT evidence isolating a consistent age-by-treatment interaction that is moderated specifically by frailty/life expectancy is limited, so the precise age/frailty interaction is not convincingly established in the literature; G4 FALSE — cascade: G5 also FALSE. G5: FALSE — because of limited high-quality trial evidence tying age+frailty to differential net benefit, the hypothesis does not yet support a definitive, widely-applicable age-based treatment rule without adding frailty measures and further evidence.
scored_features.justification: Decisive gate: G4 FALSE — age/frailty mechanisms are plausible and likely modify net effect (G2/G3 TRUE), but RCT evidence specifically confirming an age-by-frailty treatment interaction sufficient to underpin clinical rules is limited.
